subject: camel spider solifuge
title: Soldiers Swore This Spider Chased Them and Ate Camels. The Truth Is Stranger

scenes.text: Soldiers in Iraq swore this thing chased them across the desert. They were half right.
The camel spider is not a spider, not a scorpion, and not venomous. It is an arachnid with jaws up to a third of its body length.
Legends said it ran 30 miles an hour, jumped three feet, screamed, and ate the stomachs of camels. None of that is true.
What is true: it runs about 10 miles an hour, and it does run straight at people.
Not to attack. It is chasing your shadow. In the desert heat it sprints for the nearest shade, and you are carrying some.
Stop, and it stops too, resting in your shade. Then it goes back to eating insects, lizards and small birds, sawn to pulp with those jaws.

description:
Camel spiders, or solifuges, are desert arachnids that are neither spiders nor scorpions. They grow to about 15 cm, carry jaws up to one third of their body length, and have no venom, though the bite is painful.
During the 2003 Iraq war, stories spread online of camel spiders running 30 mph, jumping, screaming and eating camels and sleeping soldiers; forced-perspective photos made them look half the size of a person. In reality they run about 10 mph and follow moving people to stay in their shadow, out of the sun. They eat insects, lizards, rodents and small birds, chopping prey to pulp and liquefying it with digestive fluids.

first_comment: It looks like it has ten legs, but two of them are sensory feelers called pedipalps. There are more than 1,000 species. Which animal legend should we fact-check next?
